topics.name: Countable and uncountable: much, many, a few, a little
Conjunctions so, because, although, when, while

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: Traders brought the recipe to India.
Traders bringed the recipe to India.
Traders brung the recipe to India.
questions.rule: Bring is irregular: bring - brought - brought.

options: Add a little salt to the dough.
Add a few salt to the dough.
Add many salt to the dough.
questions.rule: Salt is uncountable, so use a little, not 'a few' or 'many'.

options: I ate a aloo samosa at the station.
I ate an aloo samosa at the station.
I ate the aloo samosa at an station.
questions.rule: Use an before a vowel sound (an aloo samosa) and a/the before 'station'.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: much ... than compares two things, so use the comparative: smaller.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: In the 16th century is the past, so use the simple past: brought.

Important begins with a vowel sound, so use an.
Subject + past verb + object + place: We fried the samosas in hot oil.

chat: Isha
Which is bigger, a Punjabi samosa or a Bengali shingara?
options: A Punjabi samosa is more big.
questions.rule: Comparing two things: big - bigger (double the g, add -er).

chat: Mom
Do we need any chutney for the samosas?
options: Yes, we need a little chutney.
Yes, we need a few chutney.
questions.rule: Chutney is uncountable, so use a little.

options: Although the samosa came from Persia, but India made it famous.
Although the samosa came from Persia, so India made it famous.
Although the samosa came from Persia, India made it famous.
questions.rule: Although already joins the two parts, so don't add 'but' or 'so'.

options: Tea tastes more good with a hot samosa.
Tea tastes gooder with a hot samosa.
Tea tastes better with a hot samosa.
questions.rule: Good is irregular: good - better - best.

questions.rule: Potatoes can be counted, so use many, not much.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Irresistible starts with a vowel sound, so use an.

questions.after: sail for India in the 14th century.
questions.rule: Set is irregular and stays the same: set - set - set.
So joins a reason to its result; 'because of' and 'despite' need a noun, not a clause.
Peas can be counted, so use a few.
Old begins with a vowel sound, so it takes an: an old snack.

chat: Dev
Where did you eat samosas yesterday?
options: I eated them at the school canteen.
I ate them at the school canteen.
I have ate them at the school canteen.
questions.rule: Eat is irregular: eat - ate - eaten.

chat: Tara
Why didn't you eat the samosa?
options: I didn't eat it because it were too spicy.
I didn't eat it because of it was too spicy.
I didn't eat it because it was too spicy.
questions.rule: Because + a clause (it was ...); 'because of' needs only a noun. It takes was.

options: The samosa travelled along trade routes and reached India.
The samosa travelled along trade routes and reach India.
The samosa travel along trade routes and reached India.
questions.rule: Two past actions joined by and both take the past: travelled ... reached.

options: There is a few oil left, but there are only a few potatoes.
There is a little oil left, but there are only a few potatoes.
There is a little oil left, but there are only a little potatoes.
questions.rule: A little with uncountable nouns (oil); a few with plural countable nouns (potatoes).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The story is in the past (were frying), so use the simple past: made.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The second part gives the reason, so join with because; 'so' introduces a result.
The ... of all compares with many, so use the superlative: thickest.
Famous begins with a consonant sound, so use a.
Although + one idea, comma, then the main idea - with no 'but'.
Less + adjective + than compares downwards: less spicy than.

chat: Shopkeeper
How much chutney do you want?
questions.rule: How much asks about an uncountable thing (chutney), so answer a little.

chat: Kunal

options: Yes, I eat two while the band was playing.
Yes, I ate two while the band was playing.
Yes, I ate two while the band was play.
questions.rule: While + past continuous for the longer action (was playing); the short action is ate.

options: The British made the humble potato popular in the 19th century.
The British made the humble potato popular on the 19th century.
The British maked the humble potato popular in the 19th century.
questions.rule: Make is irregular: made; and centuries take in.

options: This is the most delicious samosa I have ever eaten.
This is the more delicious samosa I have ever eaten.
This is the deliciousest samosa I have ever eaten.
questions.rule: Long adjectives form the superlative with the most: the most delicious.

options: When the potato reached Indian kitchens, so cooks used it in samosas.
When the potato reach Indian kitchens, cooks used it in samosas.
When the potato reached Indian kitchens, cooks used it in samosas.
questions.rule: When joins the two parts, so no 'so'; both actions are past: reached, used.

questions.rule: Strengthen a comparative with much, not 'very'; never use 'more' with an -er word.

options: I would like a aloo samosa and a cup of tea.
I would like an aloo samosa and an cup of tea.
I would like an aloo samosa and a cup of tea.
questions.rule: An before a vowel sound (an aloo samosa); a before a consonant sound (a cup).

options: Triangles are easy to fold and seal, so the filling do not escape.
Triangles are easy to fold and seal, so the filling does not escape.
Triangles are easy to fold and seal, because of the filling does not escape.

The samosa moved from royal banquets to roadside stalls and win everyone's heart.
